---
title: "Build a phylogenetic tree"
subtitle: "Module 3 — 60 min"
---

## Choosing a method

| Method | Idea | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Distance (neighbour-joining) | tree built from pairwise distances | very fast first look |
| Maximum likelihood (IQ-TREE, RAxML) | the tree that makes the alignment most probable under a substitution model | standard choice |
| Bayesian / time-scaled (BEAST, TreeTime) | adds time and uncertainty | dating, advanced analyses |

Three choices to make: the **substitution model** (IQ-TREE tests several with `-m MFP`), the **support** (ultrafast bootstrap,
`-B 1000`) and the **root** (an outgroup: here the reference genome `TOYV1_ref`).

## Step 1 — Build the maximum-likelihood tree

```bash
iqtree2 -s results/phylo/aln.fasta -m MFP -B 1000 -T 2 --seed 1 -o TOYV1_ref --prefix results/phylo/tree -redo
```

What the options mean: `-s` alignment, `-m MFP` choose the best model automatically, `-B 1000` 1,000 ultrafast bootstrap
replicates, `-T 2` two threads, `--seed 1` reproducible result, `-o TOYV1_ref` root on the reference, `--prefix` name of the output files.

IQ-TREE writes several files; the useful ones are:

```bash
ls results/phylo/tree.*
```

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `tree.treefile` | **the tree** (Newick format, with bootstrap support) |
| `tree.iqtree` | the full report (model chosen, log-likelihood, tree in text) |
| `tree.log` | what happened during the run |

Which model was chosen?

```bash
grep "Best-fit model" results/phylo/tree.iqtree
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## About the model
With so few variable sites a simple model (such as HKY or GTR variants) is chosen; the exact choice has almost no impact here.
IQ-TREE may also warn that several sequences are **identical**: this is normal, they end up on the same branch tip.
:::

**Plan B (no IQ-TREE):** a neighbour-joining tree from SNP distances, good enough to read the course examples
(but without bootstrap support):

```bash
python3 scripts/12b_tree_fallback.py
```

## Step 2 — Draw the tree

Assign the lineages (needed for the colours), then draw the tree twice:

```bash
python3 scripts/13_lineage.py results/phylo/aln.fasta
```
```bash
python3 scripts/14_plot_tree.py results/phylo/tree.treefile --color lineage --out results/phylo/tree_lineage.png
```
```bash
python3 scripts/14_plot_tree.py results/phylo/tree.treefile --color region --out results/phylo/tree_region.png
```

(Plan B: use `results/phylo/tree.nwk` instead of `tree.treefile`.) You can also open the Newick file in
**FigTree**, **iTOL** (<https://itol.embl.de>) or **Microreact** (<https://microreact.org>).

**Questions:** do the lineages form clean groups on the tree? Where is S01?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Answer
Yes: each lineage forms its own group (clade). TV.3 and the TV.1 background genomes are close to the root; TV.2 and its two
descendants TV.2.1 and TV.2.2 form one large clade. **S01 is inside the TV.2 group**, next to OB10, OB25, OB15 and OB22 (all early
genomes of the outbreak).
:::

## Step 3 — Remove the low-quality genome and rebuild

OB24 has 23 % N. Remove it from the alignment and rebuild the tree:

```bash
seqkit grep -v -p OB24 results/phylo/aln.fasta > results/phylo/aln_clean.fasta
```
```bash
iqtree2 -s results/phylo/aln_clean.fasta -m MFP -B 1000 -T 2 --seed 1 -o TOYV1_ref --prefix results/phylo/tree_clean -redo
```

**Question:** does the tree change?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Answer
The main groups and their relationships **do not change**: OB24 was inside the TV.2.2 group, which stays the same without it.
But its position had a **lower reliability** (a lot of missing data means that it can look closer to some genomes than it
really is). Excluding it removes a source of doubt and shows that the conclusions do not depend on a poor genome.
The excluded genome and the reason must be written in the report.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
With few variable sites there is little resolution: many branches are short and some are supported weakly. A tree is only as good as
the alignment and the data behind it.
:::
